The Keate arbitration of 19 February 1870 (Klip River line with the Transvaal, giving the Transvaal the Wakkerstroom area) is on the page but moves nothing the shape shows.

133,104 km2 for 1871-1884 (one cell more than the 1856 outline on the southern edge); 27 October 1871 the district was proclaimed British as Griqualand West at the diamond fields near the Vaal-Orange junction, and in July 1876 Lord Carnarvon granted the Free State £90,000 'in full satisfaction of all claims': no land changes hands, so the shape stands.

132,191 km2 for 1885-1897: Cliopatria cuts a notch of 3 cells (759 km2) out of the Ladybrand-Ficksburg corner (27.3-27.9E, 29.4-28.9S) that was inside in 1871. The page records no cession after the 1869 Aliwal North boundary, so the 1871 outline is restored.
132,191 km2 for 1898-1899, the same outline as 1885 (same notch, same correction); the Second Boer War began on 11 October 1899.

New keyframe for 1900-1902 (Cliopatria stops at 1899): the republic's outline stays under British occupation. Lord Roberts took Bloemfontein on 13 March 1900, the state was annexed as the Orange River Colony on 28 May 1900, and the burghers kept the field for nearly two years under Christiaan de Wet; the status (occupied) is in the ledger.

ledger.note: 23 February 1854: Britain gives up the Orange River Sovereignty and the Free State is born. A royal proclamation dated 30 January 1854 renounced British dominion; the Orange River Convention was signed at Bloemfontein on 23 February 1854; representatives met on 28 March 1854 and the constitution was drafted by 18 April 1854, when the republic was declared and named the Orange Free State. The region is Transorangia between the Orange and the Vaal without the Conquered Territory.

region.text: the 'Conquered Territory': land north of the Orange River and west of the Caledon River, formerly part of Basutoland, ceded to the Free State by the Treaty of Aliwal North on 12 February 1869 (the Basotho page: the disputed area ran from present-day Wepener to Zastron; it does not define the extent by river or town)

ledger.note: March 1858: war with the Basotho. 'In February 1858, tensions rose in the Orange Free State over land', and Boshoff declared war on the Basotho on 19 March 1858 (also 22 March); the page names no battle, so the month is the declaration's. The disputed ground (the border land east of the Warden Line that later became the Conquered Territory) is the researcher's reading; the page names none.

ledger.note: 11 April 1866: the peace of Thaba Bosiu. Moshoeshoe was compelled to accept the peace of Thaba Bosiu on 11 April 1866 (the Free State page says April 1866); fighting resumed in July 1867.

ledger.note: July 1867: the Third Basotho War. 'In July 1867, the third war between the Orange Free State and the Basotho began'; the Free State overran Basotho land in 1867, leaving only Thaba Bosiu. On 12 March 1868 the British declared the Basotho Kingdom a protectorate.

Treaty of Aliwal North: Land north of the Orange River and west of the Caledon River, formerly part of Basutoland, was ceded to the Free State as the Conquered Territory (the Basotho page: 'gave the Conquered Territory to the Orange Free State', the boundary moved south to Langeberg).

region.text: northern Natal: the Natal border and the districts the Boers invaded from October 1899

ledger.note: 11 October 1899: the Free State joins the Boer invasion of Natal. The war began when Free State Boers seized a train on the Natal border. The Second Boer War page adds that Kruger's ultimatum came after the Orange Free State joined and mobilised and that the Boers invaded the Cape Colony and Natal between October 1899 and January 1900; the page names no Free State front, so the zone is the Natal ground the colony-of-natal dossier uses.

region.text: northern Natal: the Natal border and the districts the Boers invaded from October 1899

ledger.note: 28 February 1900: Ladysmith is relieved ('Buller's troops marched into Ladysmith on 28 February'). The page does not date the Free State commandos' withdrawal from Natal; the British offensive into the Free State began with Paardeberg (18-27 February 1900).

ledger.note: 13 March 1900: Lord Roberts occupies Bloemfontein. British troops under Lord Roberts occupied Bloemfontein on 13 March 1900; a proclamation annexed the state as the Orange River Colony on 28 May 1900; the burghers 'kept the field' for nearly two years. The state is drawn occupied, not British, until the Treaty of Vereeniging. [Reviewer af-07-b, 2026-10-19] Confidence 2: the page dates the occupation of Bloemfontein, not of the whole republic, which the burghers held in the field to 1902.

ledger.note: 31 May 1902: the Treaty of Vereeniging ends the occupation and the republic. British sovereignty was acknowledged by the articles of peace signed on 31 May 1902.

ledger.note: 31 May 1902: the Orange Free State ceases to exist. The republic ceased to exist as an independent Boer republic on 31 May 1902 with the Treaty of Vereeniging; it was annexed as the Orange River Colony in 1900.

zones.text: the Free State, occupied from March 1900
northern Natal, invaded from October 1899 (the Free State Boers seized a Natal train on the border on 11 October 1899): the zone of the 1899-1900 contest events

wars.outcome: The Free State joined the Transvaal in October 1899; Cronje surrendered at Paardeberg on 27 February 1900, Bloemfontein fell on 13 March, the state was annexed on 28 May 1900 and the burghers fought on until the Treaty of Vereeniging, 31 May 1902.
wars.note: The Free State page gives the same dates.

certainty.note: The Orange and Vaal rivers are the southern and northern lines (the 1854 convention), but the Basutoland frontier (the Warden Line, the treaty of 15 October 1858, the peace of 1866) was disputed and the Cliopatria outline is the modern province.
The Treaty of Aliwal North (12 February 1869) defined the Basutoland border and the Keate arbitration (19 February 1870) fixed the Transvaal line; the Orange and Vaal rivers bound the rest.

notes: Three pages opened (budget up to 5). SETTLED: life 23 February 1854 to 31 May 1902 (Cliopatria 1856-1899); capital; presidents; the 1869 Conquered Territory; 1900-1902 occupation. NOT SETTLED: (1) The extent of the Conquered Territory: neither page defines it by river or town (the Basotho page: 'from present-day Wepener to Zastron', and 'north of the Caledon, including Harrismith' for the wider area). The dossier uses the name {region: Conquered Territory}, which the gazetteer lacks; the gazetteer agent should define it as the strip of the eastern Free State between the Warden Line (Cornetspruit and the Orange River through Vechtkop to Jammerbergdrift on the Caledon) and the Caledon, the Zastron-Wepener-Ladybrand-Ficksburg country. Until then free-orange-state_1854, _1856 and the 1854/1858 events resolve to the full Cliopatria outline. (2) Cliopatria's 1885 and 1898 shapes lose a 3-cell notch around Ladybrand-Ficksburg that the pages do not explain; restored by 'adjust'. (3) The Keate arbitration of 19 February 1870 ('the Klip River was fixed as the dividing line with the Transvaal, giving the Transvaal the Wakkerstroom area') is on the Free State page but the page's geography is unclear (Wakkerstroom is a Transvaal-Natal border district, not obviously the Free State's); no event is written for it. (4) The Griqualand West dispute (diamond fields; proclaimed British 27 October 1871; £90,000 paid July 1876) moved no land the shape shows; the Cliopatria outline's west edge was not tested against the fields. (5) The 1849 Warden Line date is not on the page. (6) The Free State's Second Boer War front in the Cape (Colesberg and Stormberg area) is not on any page opened, so the only contest zone is northern Natal (a train seized on the Natal border on 11 October 1899). (7) Annexation as the Orange River Colony on 28 May 1900 is shown as occupation until 31 May 1902, matching the infobox end; a British Orange River Colony dossier (1900-1910) is needed (successor). Counterparts: basutoland (af-07-x), orange-river-colony, british-colonial-empire (exists), colony-of-natal (af-07-b). Rulers: the infobox lists five presidents and de Wet (30-31 May 1902); J. J. Venter's interim 1859-1860 and other acting presidents are not on the page. Gazetteer names needed: Conquered Territory (region). The Orange River Sovereignty is an alias of the 'Orange Free State' region in the gazetteer.
